prompt: Audit a responsive web app for Apple HIG-aligned mobile UX. At 320px the page has horizontal overflow, primary controls are 28x36px, a six-column data table clips, a modal cannot be dismissed from the keyboard, body text has 3.2:1 contrast, and the hero image is 2.4MB. Produce a prioritized remediation plan with verification steps.
assertions: Identifies horizontal overflow and tests reflow at 320 CSS pixels without relying on device-specific breakpoints.
Recommends touch targets of at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels or an equivalent expanded hit area.
Proposes a mobile-safe table strategy that preserves access to every value and action.
Requires an accessible dialog pattern with focus management, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration.
Flags 3.2:1 body-text contrast as insufficient under WCAG AA and recommends token-level correction.
Treats the 2.4MB hero as a mobile performance risk and includes responsive image and measurement guidance.

prompt: Plan mobile remediation for a desktop-first project dashboard. The sidebar stays permanently open, filters consume two rows, cards use hover-only actions, the viewport meta tag is missing, and bottom actions overlap the iPhone home indicator. Keep the product a web app rather than redesigning it as a native iOS app.
assertions: Adapts Apple HIG principles to the web instead of prescribing SwiftUI, UIKit, or native-only navigation.
Recommends compact navigation with an operable menu and retained access to all destinations.
Consolidates or progressively discloses filters while preserving clear labels and state.
Replaces hover-only interactions with touch, keyboard, and visible-focus alternatives.
Requires a correct viewport meta declaration and avoids disabling user zoom.
Uses CSS safe-area environment variables for fixed bottom controls without assuming a specific iPhone model.

prompt: Review a mobile account-recovery flow. The form uses placeholder-only labels, requests email and a one-time code in separate views, auto-advances code inputs, reports errors only with red borders, and uses a 15-second toast after success. Provide findings and acceptance criteria.
assertions: Requires persistent programmatic labels and appropriate autocomplete/input-purpose metadata.
Evaluates whether the multi-step flow preserves context, progress, and a clear way back without data loss.
Warns that forced auto-advance can disrupt editing, paste, assistive technology, and error recovery.
Requires errors to be conveyed with text and programmatic association rather than color alone.
Recommends a durable success state or user-controlled dismissal instead of relying only on a timed toast.
